item.title: [UI & Layout] Adaptive Interactive UI Elements
item.description: Users expect UI elements to respond dynamically, not just statically. Incorporating subtle animations like stretchy toggles and ambient-aware contrast ensures readability and makes interfaces feel alive and genuinely user-centric, performing optimally in diverse real-world conditions. | Fonts: Inter Regular + IBM Plex Mono | Palette: #1A1A2E #E94560 #F7F7F7 #5B5B66 | Prompt: Design a responsive toggle switch component for a financial app. Ensure it has a subtle 'stretchy' knob animation on toggle, adapts track color for accessibility in light/dark mode, and maintains an ambient contrast ratio of 7:1 minimum for both states, feeling fluid and secure.

item.title: [UI & Layout] Adaptive Interactive Elements
item.description: The challenge of ambient contrast (1,000-Nit unreadable) combined with the demand for engaging, accessible micro-interactions (stretchy toggles, button hovers) means components must be visually responsive to environment and user input. item.title: [UI & Layout] Dynamic Palette Extraction & Tailwind CSS
item.description: Designers frequently receive unformatted image assets, making precise color replication challenging for front-end development. This system automates HEX code extraction from any image, ensuring pixel-perfect brand consistency and seamless integration into CSS or Tailwind palettes. | Fonts: Inter + Fira Code | Palette: #1C1C1C #F0F0F0 #4A90E2 #E85D04 | Prompt: Analyze the provided screenshot of the proposed design. Extract the dominant 5-7 HEX codes, prioritizing brand accents, primary, and secondary UI colors. Format these as a Tailwind CSS `colors` object, including semantic names like `primary-blue`, `accent-orange`, `text-dark`, `bg-light`. Ensure the output is ready for direct `tailwind.config.js` integration, optimizing for developer handoff efficiency.
